source.title: Better with Less: A Data-Active Perspective on Pre-Training Graph Neural Networks
source.authors: Jia-Rong Xu; Ren-Hong Huang; Xin Jiang; Yuxuan Cao; Carl Yang; Chun-Ping Wang; Yang Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures graph-pretraining data selection and downstream graph-task performance. It does not test language-model held-out loss scaling or the versions’ power-law claims.
record.gate_note: The paper briefly cites language-model and other pretraining scaling work, but reports no language-model loss, parameter/token/compute scaling, or compute-optimal allocation result. Its graph-pretraining data-size results concern downstream micro F1, not the behavior named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study scales graph-pretraining data (sample count, number of graph datasets, molecule count) for GNNs and measures downstream micro F1. It reports no pretraining loss and no parameter or compute sweep, and makes no language-model measurement. V5 concerns the power-law form of loss in other modalities, so downstream F1 does not bear on it. V6 is framed for language models and their scaling, so these graph-task results are recorded under fits_no_version instead. The paper cites Kaplan et al. only to contrast graph pretraining with CV/NLP, where more data gives 'better or saturating performance'.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors identify a 'curse of big data' in GNN pretraining: more samples or graph datasets do not necessarily improve downstream performance. They conclude that APT, which selects fewer data, gives better downstream results and trains about 2.2x faster than GCC.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses graph neural networks and downstream graph-task micro F1, rather than language models and held-out cross-entropy loss.

fits_no_version.finding: For GCC and GraphCL GNNs (3–5 layers), downstream micro F1 does not rise uniformly with pretraining sample count. The convex-hull fits take the form a1 ln x/x^a2 + a3, which rises and then declines (Table 6, Figs. 6–7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In graph pretraining, downstream performance is non-monotonic in pretraining data size rather than following a power-law improvement.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding graph datasets at fixed sample size does not improve, and sometimes worsens, downstream F1, with large variance across dataset combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In graph pretraining, the composition of the data matters more than the number of datasets for downstream transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: In molecular pretraining (AttrMasking, ContextPred, GraphCL on ZINC15, evaluated on BBBP), raising the number of molecules from 1k to 100k did not monotonically improve downstream performance (Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The 'curse of big data' in downstream transfer also holds for molecular GNN pretraining.

record.problems: The reported scaling observations concern graph-pretraining data and downstream micro F1, not language-model held-out loss. The Figure 1 trends are primarily presented graphically; the text gives aggregate descriptions rather than per-dataset numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix E presents additional GCC and GraphCL figure suites across layer counts and downstream datasets, plus fitted curves for downstream performance versus sample size. These were not extracted as separate rows because they measure graph-task micro F1 rather than any claim-version outcome.

untested.parts: No pretraining-loss scaling in parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation of fits to larger runs.
Layer counts (3/4/5) are varied but loss at fixed parameter count is not compared.
No loss-scaling law is measured for graph or molecular pretraining.
No analysis of fitting choices for loss scaling laws.

missing.what: Molecular pretraining data-size sweep (1k–100k molecules) with downstream BBBP performance for three backbones
Fitted curve parameters (a1 ln x/x^a2 + a3) for downstream F1 against sample size, per dataset, for GCC and GraphCL

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from cites_only to discusses because the related-work section explicitly contrasts graph pretraining with CV/NLP scaling, including Kaplan et al. The study's own results concern GNN downstream F1, outside every version as worded.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or parameter, token, or compute sweep.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger language-model runs.
No language-model architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
Although the study concerns graph pretraining, it does not measure whether a power-law loss form holds in that modality or regime.
No language-model downstream performance versus scale or pretraining-loss analysis.
No analysis of language-model scaling-law fit choices, exponents, or compute-optimal splits.
